summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including systolic heart failure, stage IV chronic kidney disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, coronary artery disease, and chronic pain on opioids was admitted for bilateral leg swelling and pain. She presented with acute on chronic heart failure and acute kidney injury, likely due to fluid overload from excessive fluid intake and high salt consumption. Hyponatremia and encephalopathy were attributed to volume overload and medication accumulation, particularly gabapentin, which was held and later restarted at a reduced dose. Treatment with intravenous Lasix improved her volume status, renal function, and mental clarity. Her oxycodone dose was reduced, and she was discharged home on her baseline diuretic with instructions for daily weight monitoring and close follow-up. A left foot X-ray revealed soft tissue edema and a foreign body in the hallux, which was removed. She improved clinically and was discharged in stable condition.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Anemia in other chronic diseases classified elsewhere
